subject: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ recap and next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie@lifeflow.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ recap and next steps

Ellie — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so the procurement and finance teams can evaluate: 

Summary of what you said (please flag if I misremember):
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~50M tokens / month (spiky during monthly syncs).
- Current procurement budget range (target): $8k - $12k / month.
- Primary objectives: reduce per-token cost while preserving quality, tight latency needs on summary endpoints (~200-300ms p95).

Unit-econ framing we discussed (for internal alignment):
- Your target implied unit price (if evenly spread): $160 - $240 per 1M tokens given 50M tokens/mo and $8k-$12k budget.
- Current hosted benchmarks (non-exhaustive): OpenAI/Anthropic higher capability models typically sit in the high hundreds-to-thousands per 1M (see deeper matrix attached). Open-model hosts land in the low hundreds.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can procurement confirm a target committed volume range for a pilot (3 months)? e.g., 25M - 75M total tokens committed across 3 months.
2) Can you share a contact for the procurement queue (I see procurement@lifeflowhealth.com copied; if there's a portal link, send it).
3) Ben is attaching a simple model showing per-1M comparisons at three pricing bands — Ben, please call out assumptions on model size/latency tradeoffs for Lifeflow.

What Redwood is proposing (preliminary / non-binding):
- Pilot priced at $220 per 1M tokens with a 50M token committed floor across 3 months (volume discounts at 100M+). Includes basic observability and 14-day data retention.
- Optional: SOC2 + SLA add-on and private deployment options if Lifeflow needs on-prem/VPC.

I attached the benchmark PDF and the lightweight pricing model so you can plug in your numbers. If this looks directionally correct, let’s slot a 30-minute procurement + engineering sync next week (I’m available Wed/Thu mornings PT).

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

Attachments referenced: lifeflow_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (xlsx), redwood-benchmark-matrix.pdf (pdf)

From: Ellie Ramos <ellie@lifeflow.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Neal Gupta <neal@lifeflowhealth.com>, procurement@lifeflowhealth.com
Date: 2027-06-02T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ recap and next steps

Thanks, Stephanie — this is great and mostly aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Volume: 50M/mo is our mid-case. Planning range for the pilot is 30M - 70M tokens total / month (we have a couple of power users that drive spikes).
- Budget: the $8k-$12k range is for a short-term procurement band — we can stretch to $15k/mo if the SLAs and SOC2 evidence are in place.
- Target $/1M: finance would like to see options in the $150-$240 / 1M range to justify a 3-month committed pilot.

Procurement: procurement@lifeflowhealth.com is the right intake; Neal is the exec sponsor who will sign off (looped). We typically need an initial statement of work and an order form for pilot commitments. 

Can you confirm what is included in the $220 / 1M pilot price you suggested (observability, model selection, any rate-limits)? Also please send the SOC2 evidence and the SLA draft you mentioned.

— Ellie
Ellie Ramos | Head of Product, Lifeflow Health
ellie@lifeflow.ai | +1 (617) 555-0224

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie@lifeflow.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ recap and next steps

Ellie — dropping a quick model and the competitive matrix (attached). High-level notes on assumptions used in the attached spreadsheet: 

Assumptions called out in lifeflow_pricing_model_v1.xlsx:
- Workload profile: 60% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 40% long prompts (avg 1,200 tokens); 1.2x KV-cache hit assumed for summary endpoints.
- Model tiers compared: Redwood-quantized (prod), OpenAI gpt-4x-ish class, Anthropic-claude-prod, Mistral/optimized open-host variants.
- Latency SLO targets: p95 <= 300ms for short calls; longer for long prompts. Some open-host setups hit lower unit cost at the expense of higher variance in latency.

Benchmark summary (per 1M tokens, approximate):
- OpenAI (high-capability offering): $2,400 / 1M 
- Anthropic (high-capability): $1,600 / 1M
- Redwood Hosted (current list): $350 / 1M
- Open-host optimized (self-hosted/partners): $280 - $320 / 1M (depends on quantization + batching)

Redwood commercial offer for Lifeflow (proposal):
- Pilot: $220 / 1M with a 50M token committed floor (3 months). Includes: routing, basic observability dashboard, 14-day inference logs, one integrated model variant chosen for latency/cost tradeoff.
- Add-ons: SOC2 evidence packet + SLA draft available; full SOC2 + enhanced retention and private deployment are priced separately.

Why $220 works for Lifeflow: at your stated 50M tokens/mo mid-case, $220/1M gives an annual run-rate of ~$132k (if you convert to a committed annual view) — this allows us to justify reserved capacity and predictable latency, while still being materially below hosted high-capability rates.

I attached the spreadsheet and the benchmark PDF. I also included a simple sensitivity table (tab "sensitivity") that maps cost per 1M to monthly spend across 30M/50M/70M ranges so procurement can see how the price shifts.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: lifeflow_pricing_model_v1.xlsx, redwood-benchmark-matrix.pdf, SLA-draft-v2.pdf

Hi team — procurement here. Quick checklist items for an initial order form and pilot approval: 

1) Signed order form (we can accept DocuSign) 
2) Pilot SOW (1 page minimum) and the SLA draft (please attach the redlined SLA we can send to legal) 
3) SOC2 Type II report (latest) and any pen-test summaries you can share under NDA.
4) Invoice details and payment terms (Net 30; we can discuss prepay if needed).

If Redwood can provide the items above this week, we can route a pilot PO and target a start date ~June 21. Otherwise the procurement queue pushes to July.

Please attach the DocuSign and SOC2 link in reply and we will kick the internal approval.
